Is there any way we can test whether we are in a simulated reality or physical universe?

I would say no.

Since I'm going to go on for a bit, I'll start out with a TL:DR version: it's possible that all of Neo's experiences of being freed from the Matrix then learning to take advantage of the simulation were, themselves, simulated.

The possibility that we're in a simulation was originally posited (it actually dates back, though in a somewhat different form, to Descartes' "evil demon") to make a point about human perception. It wasn't a serious speculation, but an illustration of a limitation of human perception.

Reality is not directly experienced. It quite simply cannot ever be directly experienced. That's not a "failure" that science can somehow overcome, but an ineradicable part of human existence.

Your eyes don't see. Your ears don't hear. Your fingers don't feel. In each and all cases, they (apparently) simply take in sensory data and communicate it to the mind, then the mind interprets it. Your mind is the thing that's actually seeing and hearing and feeling. That's where all of the perception actually takes place, and that's simply the way it is. That was the thing that Descartes recognized and illustrated with the evil demon. The fact that all perception actually occurs within the mind means that it's possible that false data could be fed to the mind (by the evil demon in Descartes' version, by a computer network in the modern update), and the mind would have no way of knowing if that was the case or not, since the mind is the only thing that perceives reality and the data it receives is the only thing from which it can build that perception. The two are inextricably interlocked and interdependent yet distinct from each other, and there's simply no way around that. Again, it's not some sort of failing that might be overcome by science, but a simple and unavoidable fact of the human experience.

Any and all data that might be gathered by any mechanism by which one might seek to test if perceived reality is simulated would necessarily go through that same process. It could not be directly perceived - it would (apparently) be recorded by the eyes and ears and skin, then communicated to the mind, which would interpret it. So the mechanism whereby any such test might be done and the data gathered by any such test would necessarily be subject to the possibility of simulation itself. And it's simply impossible to get away from that. The gap between perception and conception cannot be bridged.
